files.pkg/source/Main.brs:
sub Main()
    screen = CreateObject("roSGScreen")
    port = CreateObject("roMessagePort")
    screen.setMessagePort(port)
    screen.CreateScene("AppScene")
    screen.show()
    while true
        msg = wait(0, port)
        if type(msg) = "roSGScreenEvent" and msg.isScreenClosed() then return
    end while
end sub

declared.rules: A Roku app written in TypeScript and TSX on Roku's RSG 2.0 SDK, with SolidJS through @roku-sdk/solid (never solid-js, never React). It runs on Roku OS 15.1 and later, in Hermes beside SceneGraph's render thread, and draws SceneGraph nodes: no HTML, CSS, DOM or WebGL. src/index.ts registers the app's one anchor node, App in src/components/App.tsx (defineAnchorNode, extending FocusBoundaryBase), which src/compiled-components/AppScene.xml holds; pkg/ goes into the package as it is (pkg/source/Main.brs starts the scene). Write the app in src/ as plain SolidJS components under that anchor node, with lowercase SceneGraph node tags (rectangle, label, poster, group, layoutGroup, video, audio, timer) or @roku-sdk/components. Before writing, read the SDK's own guides for what you're doing, in .agents/skills/roku-sdk-*/SKILL.md (Lamp installs them with the app's packages): roku-sdk-solid-on-roku and roku-sdk-sdk-components every time, roku-sdk-focus-management for anything the remote moves through, and roku-sdk-screen-navigation, roku-sdk-fetch-and-data-loading, roku-sdk-data-entry-keyboards, roku-sdk-dialogs-and-modals, roku-sdk-flex-grid, roku-sdk-slideshow, roku-sdk-effects or roku-sdk-fonts-and-glyphs when they apply. Their guides to devices, MCP, the CLI and packaging aren't for you: Lamp builds the app and puts it on the Roku. Import SolidJS (createSignal, createEffect, createMemo, onMount, For, Show) from @roku-sdk/solid; iterate with <For>, never .map() in JSX; read props and signals inside JSX, a memo or an effect, and never destructure props. Focus: the remote's keys reach the RootFocusBoundary in App.tsx through keyEvent, and its initialFocus must name something focusable; wrap each region in a FocusBoundary with navigation "vertical", "horizontal" or "grid", make each item useFocusable (attach its ref, draw its focus from isFocused()) and handle OK in its onKey with onPress; leave the arrows to the boundaries. Key names are up, down, left, right, OK, back, play, rewind, fastforward, options, replay. Back that nothing handles leaves the app, so on a screen past the first, handle back to go back. The screen is 1920x1080: keep content inside a 5% safe margin, text at least 28px, a dark background, and focus that's plain from across the room. Network requests use the runtime's fetch with one argument: fetch(url), or fetch(new Request(url, { method, headers, body })) with a string body for anything else; check response.ok, since an error status still resolves. Saved data goes through Lamp's LampStore, never the registry directly: Roku keeps about 32 KB of saved data per channel, shared by every app Lamp puts on that Roku, so keep it small. Pictures the app ships go in src/ and are imported (import { uri } from "../images/fox.png"), never named by a pkg:/ path; a timer for animation or a game loop is setInterval or a timer node, never a busy loop. A package the app needs goes in package.json's dependencies at an exact version, @roku-sdk ones at the version the others are on: Lamp installs them before your next turn and every build, so never run pnpm, npm, npx or rk yourself. Lamp builds with Roku's rk, which type-checks first: a type error fails the build and comes back to you to fix. roku-config.ts's manifestEntries name the icon and splash pictures Lamp draws in pkg/images (mm_icon_focus_hd, mm_icon_focus_fhd, splash_screen_sd, splash_screen_hd, splash_screen_fhd, at icon_focus_hd.png, icon_focus_fhd.png, splash_sd.png, splash_hd.png and splash_fhd.png): keep those entries, add them when they're missing, and never draw or replace those files. A screensaver is an app of its own: manifestEntries adds screensaver_title (the app's title) and pkg/source/Main.brs a sub RunScreenSaver() that shows AppScene the way Main does (keep Main, so it can be opened and tried); the person picks it under Settings, Theme, Screensaver. Keep it slow and dark, and move what it shows now and then. console.log writes to the Roku's log. When the Roku's log says the app "is not permitted to run TypeScript", the Roku lacks the device token from Roku that its SDK's apps need during Roku's beta: say exactly that, not that it needs an update, since nothing in the app or its version fixes it. Lamp's support library is in src/lamp and is built with the app.
